cards.title: Accops for Government: Zero Trust Reference Architecture, Seven Integrated Components (2026 V2)
cards.key_problem: A government organisation hardening its IT needs one Zero Trust design covering private application access, identity, isolated desktops, internet browsing, cross-network file transfer, remote IT support and endpoints - replacing VPNs, NAC, WAF and separate access portals rather than bolting on seven point products.
key_outcomes: Seven 'off the shelf' components in one reference architecture: ZTNA, HyID (MFA/SSO/IAM), VDI Suite, Remote Browser Isolation, AirBridge, Huddle and HyDesk thin clients - each with capabilities, a reference architecture diagram and use cases

ZTNA replaces VPN with identity- and application-level access: Layer 7 reverse proxy, Layer 4 tunnelling, device posture, context policies, clientless or agent access, DLP (copy-paste, screenshot, screen-recording blocks) and support for external QRNG for post-quantum cryptography
Web application protection against OWASP Top 10, OWASP Top 20 automated threats and SANS Top 25

Four ZTNA deployment options - on-premises or cloud, each direct-connect or reverse-connect via Edge and App Connectors with no inbound firewall ports - and two models: self-hosted or ZTNA-as-a-service
HyID: OTP, push, biometrics, hardware tokens, QR passwordless login, FIDO and Windows Hello, SAML 2.0/OAuth SSO, RADIUS connectors, impossible-travel detection, device binding, SIEM integration
VDI for developers, auditors, external vendors (time-bound sandboxes with auto-reset) and privileged admins, with session recording, USB/screen-capture blocking and non-persistent desktops

Remote Browser Isolation streams only pixels; AirBridge moves files between isolated networks with multi-engine AV scanning and Content Disarm and Reconstruction; Huddle gives on-premise remote support that works in air-gapped networks
cards.brief: A nine-page, component-by-component solution document written as a proposal for 'Government Organisations'. Each of the seven components gets a product overview, key capabilities, a reference architecture diagram and a use-case list. ZTNA is the most detailed section (deployment topologies, flexible model, seven use cases including VPN replacement and consolidating VPN/NAC/WAF/portals). The VDI section is the one to point at for privileged access, auditor and third-party developer scenarios; Browser Isolation plus AirBridge covers internet-to-internal separation; Huddle and HyDesk cover remote support and endpoint replacement. No customers, prices or statistics are cited. Its content is the same as the SharePoint 'Accops Solutions for Govt. V1 '26' (differences are typesetting and a few words).
cards.use_for: Send to a government, PSU or public-sector prospect - or attach to a tender/RFP response - when they need the full architecture in one document: VPN replacement with ZTNA, air-gapped or isolated networks, secure file transfer between networks, internet isolation, or thin-client rollouts. This is the public, sendable edition.
cards.needs_human: Same content as the SharePoint 'Accops Solutions for Govt. V1 '26.pdf' (carded internal in batch-05, re-typeset May 2026, after this March 2026 PDF). Confirm which is canonical; if the SharePoint file is the same document, its card can point reps at this public URL.

cards.title: Accops HySecure Gateway Datasheet (V4, Aug 2025)
cards.key_problem: Remote, on-premises and third-party users need access to every kind of internal application without exposing backend servers or putting users on a flat network, under one gateway that also protects the web applications behind it.
key_outcomes: Zero Trust access with continuous identity and device-posture verification, ABAC and just-in-time access provisioning

Application coverage: web, TCP and UDP client-server, dynamic-port apps, file shares, RDP virtual channels, VoIP, VDI via HyWorks, published subnets, and SaaS (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce)
TLS 1.3 and quantum-safe encryption algorithms; RSA 2048/4096; DDoS protection; hardened gateway OS

Web Application Protection: OWASP Top 10, OWASP Top 20 automated threats, SANS 25, 4000+ built-in signatures, AI-scored bot protection, API/XML/GraphQL/WebSocket validation, built-in AV scan plus ICAP
Device identification on over 20 parameters (CPUID, MBID, HDDID, MACID, IMEI and more); tamper-protected agent; clipboard, print and USB restriction; geo-fencing
Authentication incl. biometrics, push consent, FIDO2/WebAuthn passwordless, OAuth/OpenID Connect, Google Secure LDAP without Active Directory, RSA SecurID or third-party OTP

Three deployment topologies: inbound ZTNA on-premises, reverse-connect via the Accops ZTNA Cloud Plane, or reverse-connect 100% on-premises/private cloud with no inbound firewall openings; runs on bare metal, VMware ESXi, XenServer, Hyper-V, Nutanix AHV, Proxmox, Red Hat OpenShift, AWS, Azure, Oracle Cloud, Google Cloud and Kubernetes
cards.brief: The full eight-page HySecure Gateway specification: product overview, then feature lists for application support, access security (including a long Web Application Protection section), management, authentication, auditing, authorisation, endpoint control, access modes (HyLite HTML5 clientless, agent, full client, iOS/Android, L3 VPN with the new Turbo Tunnel, reverse proxy, site-to-site, built-in RDP gateway) and platform support, followed by three deployment-topology diagrams with explanations and a conclusion. A word-level diff shows the extracted text is identical to the public V5 2026 datasheet - V5 changes only the layout and adds a 2026 copyright line.
cards.use_for: Prefer V5 2026 - same content in the newer edition. This V4 is only worth sending if a customer has already been given this URL and asks for it again.
cards.stale_risk: The body carries no date; '2025' comes from 'Aug 25' in the filename (the PDF itself was re-exported in February 2026). Its content is word-for-word the same as V5 2026, so nothing in it is outdated, but a customer comparing the two will see an older version number.
cards.superseded_by: public/Accops Hysecure Datasheet V5 2026.pdf - word-for-word the same datasheet (verified by text diff); V5 is the newer 2026 edition. Send V5.

cards.title: Accops Digital Workspace: Integrated Platform Brochure with Full Datasheet (V2, 2026)
cards.key_problem: Delivering secure work-from-anywhere usually means buying remote access, application virtualisation, VDI, MFA, identity federation, SSO and thin clients from different vendors and making them work together.
key_outcomes: One integrated, modular suite for remote access, app and desktop virtualisation (VDI), MFA, identity federation, SSO and thin clients
SPAN technology for remote access from any device, even over slow high-latency networks, with endpoint trust scored before access and location-based policies
Secure sandbox controlling clipboard, printing, session recording, file saving, USB and internet access, relaxing automatically at trusted locations
User productivity and experience monitoring (log-on/log-off, per-application time, app response time) plus privileged access audit and control
Scales to thousands of users: Active-Active N+1 cluster, built-in load balancing, DR mode with client-side failover

Datasheet table: session desktops on Windows RDS 2016-2025 and Ubuntu; dedicated Windows 10/11, Ubuntu 22 and RHEL 9 desktops; VMware, Nutanix AHV/Prism Central, Hyper-V/SCVMM, Azure and physical desktops; watermarking, session recording, SIEM support, FIDO and passwordless logon
cards.brief: The platform brochure for Accops Digital Workspace in two halves. Pages 1-4 give the platform story and twelve feature sections (virtual desktop provisioning with linked and full clones and SysPrep, zero-trust remote access, endpoint control, integrated application delivery from RDS/App-V, built-in IAM with MFA/SSO and risk alerts, auditing, secure sandbox, device management, enterprise mobility for BYOD and vendors, productivity monitoring, privileged access, scalability). Pages 4-8 are a category-by-category datasheet: publishing, hypervisors, application support, device and system management, session policies, desktop provisioning, entitlements, endpoint control, network security, access methods (including Nano LIVE USB and HyLite), monitoring, deployment and authorisation. No customer names, statistics or analyst claims. Text is near-identical to the 2025 edition: the cover line changed and the closing drops 'Made-in-India'.
cards.use_for: First meeting or follow-up with a prospect who has not yet picked a product - the platform story and the full capability table in one sendable PDF. Also useful for an RFP where the buyer wants the combined VDI + ZTNA + MFA + thin client feature list.
cards.stale_risk: The datasheet's Network Security row still says 'Version upto TLS1.2', while the HySecure V5 2026 datasheet claims TLS 1.3 and quantum-safe algorithms; its hypervisor list omits Proxmox, which other 2026 material supports; and the Deployment row reads 'Hyper-V virtualization platforms from VMware, XenServer, Hyper-V'. Quote HySecure specifics from the HySecure datasheet, not from here.
cards.needs_human: Ask marketing to update the datasheet table to TLS 1.3 and add Proxmox (and fix the garbled Deployment line) in the next edition.
